usefulness.rationale: Understanding is high: the dossier converges from many independent sources (Wikipedia, New Yorker, BBC Reith Lectures PDF, Library of Congress, publisher pages, reviews) on a coherent picture of Adichie — Nigerian writer born 15 September 1977, author of Purple Hibiscus, Half of a Yellow Sun, Americanah, The Thing Around Your Neck, the We Should All Be Feminists talk/essay, MacArthur Fellowship 2008, American Academy 2017, Reith Lecturer 2022, and recent work including Dream Count — all matching the identity anchors. Conversation readiness is strong: a reader gets her works, awards, stated views (on post-colonial theory, feminism, the US left), connections (Wole Soyinka, Dave Eggers, Beyoncé sampling), and recent personal context (parents' deaths, son's death, twins, Dream Count at the 2025 National Book Festival). Remaining questions is low: the dossier never states what it does not know — there is no explicit gaps or limitations section; uncertainty is only implicit in 'contested' status flags, and several statements rest on truncated headline or title-only quotes without acknowledging the thinness. Overclaims found are mostly statements adding specifics (a prize name, a title name, an age, a publisher/date, an evaluative label) that their cited excerpt does not contain; none match the listed unjustified conclusions (no registrar or 67-books claim appears in the dossier).
